text: { "entries": [ { "name_han": "中岳嵩高灵庙碑", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: sacred geography and stele-writing prove that mountain-temple cults are not mere local piety but official-cosmic contracts binding Heaven, Earth, and the state. The text demonstrates that ritual inscription at Zhongyue (Songshan) legitimizes both Daoist lineage and imperial authority by making the mountain a permanent witness of cosmic order.", "logic_chain": "1) Songshan is the central peak among the Five Sacred Mountains → 2) therefore it mediates the axis of Heaven–Earth qi → 3) a stele at the Lingmiao records offerings and revelations as public evidence → 4) evidence of numinous response (lingying) proves the mountain’s agency → 5) agency of the mountain validates the cult and the sponsors’ virtue → 6) conclusion: political and spiritual legitimacy flow from correctly situating ritual at the cosmic center.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi, treat ‘center’ (Earth, ji-wu) as the pivot that balances other stems; diagnose when center qi is missing or over-strong. 2) For cultivation, use Songshan/central-mountain imagery as a meditation axis (middle dantian / yellow court). 3) When reading temple omens or ‘response’ stories, map them to day-master resonance with Earth/central palace. 4) Prefer stele-style dating (year, stem-branch, ritual intent) when reconstructing historical charts. 5) Use ‘inscription as contract’ logic: a vow or talisman is only valid if place, time, and sponsor virtue align.", "logic_compare": "Unlike the West Peak Huashan stele, which emphasizes martial-apotropaic and border-mountain power, this text centers axial/central mediation. Unlike pure Daoist hagiography, it is a public stone contract between cult, mountain, and polity—hence more juridical and cosmographic than narrative." }, { "name_han": "太平御览·道部", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: encyclopedic classification of the Dao proves that the Way is not one school’s monopoly but a state-legible system of categories—immortals, methods, mountains, texts—through which power and knowledge are ordered. Differs from later fiction anthologies by claiming court-level knowledge control instead of entertainment or moral parable." }, { "name_han": "册府元龟·帝王部·符瑞", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: portents (fuyui) prove that Heaven’s mandate is legible in material anomalies, and that correct imperial response converts omen into political capital. The section argues that legitimacy is not abstract philosophy but a feedback loop of sign → interpretation → ritual/policy.", "logic_chain": "1) Heaven communicates through irregular phenomena → 2) only the sovereign is the proper addressee of those signs → 3) officials archive and classify signs as evidence of virtue or warning → 4) correct recognition and response reaffirm the mandate → 5) misreading or ignoring signs justifies critique or crisis → 6) conclusion: political time is omen-time; history is a ledger of cosmic replies.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi yearly luck, treat ‘unusual’ combinations (void, clash of key gods) as fuyui requiring response, not fatalism. 2) Practice omen protocol: observe → classify (auspicious/warning) → act (remedy, timing, conduct). 3) Map imperial ‘response rites’ onto personal cultivation (confession, offering, schedule change). 4) When charts show strong Fire/Heaven-official patterns, weight public reputation and mandate-like career signs. 5) Train interpretation ethics: do not invent omens; read only what the chart actually produces.", "logic_compare": "Unlike 玉海·郊祀, which focuses on standardized state sacrifice, this text prioritizes extraordinary signs as proof of mandate. Unlike literary 灵异 collections, its purpose is statecraft historiography, not wonder or fiction." }, { "name_han": "玉海·郊祀", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: suburban sacrifice (jiaosi) proves that cosmic order is maintained by calendarized, graded ritual to Heaven and Earth rather than by ad hoc devotion. The text demonstrates that correct space (south suburb), time (solstice cycles), and rank of offering are the logical conditions of political-cosmic equilibrium.", "logic_chain": "1) Heaven and Earth require periodic, formal address → 2) the south suburb is the spatial analog of Heaven’s seat → 3) solstice and seasonal nodes are the temporal keys → 4) ritual ranks and utensils encode hierarchy of cosmos and court → 5) when form is complete, qi and politics realign → 6) conclusion: cosmic stability is a function of exact ritual geometry and timing.", "logic_practice": "1) Align BaZi remedies and offerings with solar terms (jieqi), not only lunar festivals. 2) Treat day-master ‘audience with Heaven’ as jiaosi: use hours/directions that match the chart’s noble gods. 3) For cultivation, schedule major work at winter/summer solstice poles (yin-yang extremes). 4) Design ritual space: facing, height, purity rules as micro-jiaosi. 5) Diagnose disorder as mis-timed or mis-ranked action (wrong god, wrong season).", "logic_compare": "Differs from 符瑞 by stressing regular liturgy over irregular omen. Differs from mountain steles by locating the main cosmic contract at the capital’s ritual periphery rather than at a sacred peak." }, { "name_han": "天中记", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: a late Ming leishu proves that ‘Heaven’s center’ knowledge is a collage of classical, historical, and marvel materials organized for retrieval—authority comes from breadth of citation and topical order. Compared with pure fiction collections, it still claims encyclopedic utility rather than story art alone." }, { "name_han": "艺文类聚·灵异部", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: collecting ‘numinous anomalies’ for literary encyclopedias proves that the strange is a category of culture useful for rhetoric, omen literacy, and moral illustration—not only for priests. The section demonstrates that anomaly becomes classical capital when excerpted and re-usable.", "logic_chain": "1) Literature needs figures of the uncanny → 2) court compilers excerpt historical and legendary marvels → 3) marvels are sorted as a genus (lingyi) → 4) genus status makes them teachable and citable → 5) citation in essays/poetry trains readers to read signs → 6) conclusion: the supernatural is domesticated into elite knowledge through anthology form.", "logic_practice": "1) Train BaZi intuition on classical ‘strange correspondences’ (dreams, animals, weather) as symbolic language. 2) Separate literary omen from technical rule: use 灵异 for metaphor, classics for calculation. 3) In client counseling, use story exempla to explain clash/combine without fatalism. 4) Catalog recurring anomaly motifs against ten-gods patterns. 5) Practice critical filter: aesthetic value ≠ predictive validity.", "logic_compare": "Unlike 册府符瑞, it serves literary culture more than mandate politics. Unlike Qing zhiguai fiction, it is excerpt-based and non-novelistic, aiming at classifiable snippets for composition." }, { "name_han": "剪灯新话", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: early Ming chuanqi proves that after dynastic rupture, the underworld, ghosts, and retributive law become the narrative court where human justice fails—fiction argues that moral causality is stricter than official law. Love and exam ambition are tested against ghostly contract and karmic ledger.", "logic_chain": "1) Human courts and exams are corruptible → 2) the dead and spirits retain memory of debt and vow → 3) narrative stages encounters that enforce unpaid justice → 4) protagonists who honor vows/rituals survive or transform → 5) those who break faith suffer retributive plot turns → 6) conclusion: ethical law is cosmic; fiction is its courtroom drama.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi ethics counseling, stress vow-keeping and debt-clearing as luck factors (not only gods). 2) Read Peach Blossom / Officer patterns with 剪灯-style caution: desire without ritual form invites ghostly backlash metaphors. 3) Use story structure for timing: crisis → ritual recognition → resolution as luck-cycle template. 4) For cultivation, practice ‘clearing unfinished business’ (apology, offering, ending false vows). 5) Distinguish entertainment omen from chart evidence when clients bring ghost dreams.", "logic_compare": "More structured and literati than later oral-flavored Qing zhiguai; less encyclopedic than leishu. Differs from 耳食录 by stronger early-Ming exam-and-ghost moral architecture rather than Qing social satire." }, { "name_han": "耳食录", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: Qing ‘hearsay’ tales prove that social rumor and strange events are a diagnostic mirror of class hypocrisy, desire, and local power—truth is what people dare only say as ghost story. The text argues that the supernatural is a coded sociology.", "logic_chain": "1) Direct critique of officials/customs is risky → 2) hearsay frame distances the author → 3) spirits, foxes, and anomalies act out social tensions → 4) readers decode moral targets from plot outcomes → 5) ‘ear-eating’ (credulous listening) is both method and warning → 6) conclusion: strange tales are a critical epistemology of Qing society.", "logic_practice": "1) When charts show strong Seal/Officer imbalance, look for social-role stress (as in 耳食 satire). 2) Treat client anecdotes as hearsay data: useful, biased, to be verified against stems-branches. 3) Use fox/ghost motifs as metaphors for hidden attachments and parasitism in relationships. 4) Practice ethical listening without superstition inflation. 5) For cultivation, purify ‘hearsay mind’—don’t let rumor qi steer decisions.", "logic_compare": "Unlike 剪灯新话’s elegant chuanqi of retribution, it is more anecdotal and socially pointed. Unlike 谐铎, it is less systematically ‘bell of harmony’ moral essay-tale hybrid." }, { "name_han": "谐铎", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: ‘the harmonious bell’ proves that comedy, irony, and strange episodes can ring a moral alarm louder than solemn preaching—wit is a logical instrument of reform. The collection argues that exposing absurdity realigns human conduct with cosmic decency.", "logic_chain": "1) Didactic seriousness often fails to change behavior → 2) humorous or bizarre frames lower defenses → 3) punchline reveals ethical inversion → 4) inversion shocks the reader into revaluation → 5) revaluation is the true ‘sounding of the bell’ → 6) conclusion: satire is a spiritual technology of awakening.", "logic_practice": "1) In counseling, use gentle irony to break fatalistic BaZi readings without shaming. 2) Map ‘absurd outcomes’ in charts (wealth god hurting self) as 谐铎 inversions teaching balance. 3) Cultivation practice: daily ‘bell’—one honest laugh at ego’s tricks. 4) When Hurt Officer is strong, channel it into constructive critique, not chaos. 5) Prefer corrective stories over scare tactics in ethical timing advice.", "logic_compare": "More intentionally satirical-moral than 夜雨秋灯录’s sentimental/strange romance. Differs from 耳食录 by a clearer program of ‘sounding the bell’ reform through wit." }, { "name_han": "夜雨秋灯录", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: late Qing tale-collections under rain-and-lamp atmosphere prove that emotion, fate, and the uncanny intertwine in a world of social decline—feeling (qing) itself becomes a causal force. The text argues that destiny is experienced as night-listening: partial, intimate, and rain-blurred.", "logic_chain": "1) Public institutions weaken in late Qing imagination → 2) private rooms (lamp, rain) become sites of revelation → 3) ghosts and coincidences answer suppressed emotions → 4) narrative prioritizes pathos over system → 5) pathos trains readers to see fate as lived texture → 6) conclusion: cosmic pattern is known through affective encounter, not only through official omen tables.", "logic_practice": "1) Weight emotional houses (Spouse, Peer, Output) carefully in late-style ‘qing’ cases. 2) Night-hour charts / yin gods: use gentle language, not harsh decree. 3) Cultivation: rain-lamp meditation—observe arising images without grasping. 4) Timing advice for grief years: ritual + rest, not aggressive remedy stacking. 5) Convert story pathos into chart factors (void, clash of resource/seal as loneliness markers).", "logic_compare": "More lyrical and late-Qing than early Ming 剪灯. Less purely satirical than 谐铎; more ‘mood of decline’ than 萤窗异草’s often ornate romance-anomaly craft." }, { "name_han": "右台仙馆笔记", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: Yu Yue’s notes prove that literati skepticism and documentary habit can host the strange without surrendering critical judgment—anomaly is recorded as problem for reason. The text argues for a scholarly middle path: neither credulous fangshi nor pure denial.", "logic_chain": "1) Elite learning prizes evidence and philology → 2) strange reports still circulate among officials and scholars → 3) notebook form allows provisional storage without dogma → 4) commentary weighs probability and motive → 5) residual unexplained cases remain open → 6) conclusion: rational culture strengthens itself by carefully archiving the residual.", "logic_practice": "1) Adopt 右台 method in BaZi: record cases, mark confidence levels, revise. 2) Separate observation, inference, and client belief in write-ups. 3) Cultivation: ‘notebook mind’—register experiences without inflating them into enlightenment claims. 4) When classic rules fail, archive counterexamples instead of forcing fit. 5) Prefer provisional language in predictions (ranges, conditions).", "logic_compare": "More scholarly and restrained than commercial zhiguai like 夜雨秋灯录. Differs from imperial omen books by personal literati epistemology rather than mandate ideology." }, { "name_han": "萤窗异草", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: ‘strange grasses by the firefly window’ proves that Qing talent-and-beauty aesthetics can absorb the supernatural into refined narrative craft—anomaly serves romance, talent, and fate of the refined self. It argues that destiny is readable in the chemistry of qing, talent, and otherworldly aid or trial.", "logic_chain": "1) Literati identity centers talent and sentiment → 2) foxes/immortals/ghosts become partners or examiners of that identity → 3) plots test constancy of feeling and study → 4) otherworldly reward or punishment ratifies human worth → 5) ornamental prose elevates the strange to art → 6) conclusion: the cosmos sponsors refined self-realization when qing and talent align.", "logic_practice": "1) For charts with strong Output + Peach Blossom, read ‘talent-qing’ paths carefully. 2) Treat ‘immortal aid’ motifs as Resource/Seal support patterns. 3) Cultivation: firefly-window practice—short night sessions of study + calm breath. 4) Warn against romanticizing spirit-relationships when Officer/Kill is unstable. 5) Use story arcs to explain ten-year luck as chapters of trial and recognition.", "logic_compare": "More ornate and romance-centered than 耳食录’s social hearsay; less encyclopedic than leishu. Compared with 剪灯新话, it is Qing taste—longer on sentiment and polish than early-Ming moral court-of-ghosts structure." }, { "name_han": "西岳华山庙碑", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: the Huashan temple stele proves that the Western Peak is a juridical-numinous power that polices borders of life, death, and imperial space—stone text makes the mountain an enforcer of oaths and a guarantor of regional order. Legitimacy is forged by naming the mountain’s office and past responses.", "logic_chain": "1) Huashan occupies the west metal position in the Five Peaks system → 2) west encodes weapons, autumn, judgment, and boundary → 3) temple cult archives petitions and miracles → 4) stele freezes that archive into permanent law-like memory → 5) rulers and locals both claim protection under that memory → 6) conclusion: sacred mountain office is a political-cosmic police power, not mere scenery.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi, link strong Metal / west / You-Xu patterns to Huashan-type ‘judgment and boundary’ themes. 2) Oath and contract work: use metal hours/directions for cutting bad ties. 3) Cultivation: white-metal breathing, decluttering, decisive endings. 4) Remedies for chaotic Peach Blossom: invoke ‘boundary god’ logic—clear rules. 5) Historical dating of events: match stele years to stem-branch for macro cases.", "logic_compare": "Unlike Zhongyue’s central-axis mediation, Huashan stresses western martial-legal numen. Unlike Taishan’s imperial tour inscriptions, it is temple-cult and regional-oath focused as much as imperial cosmology." }, { "name_han": "泰山刻石", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: Qin (and related) Taishan inscriptions prove that ascending the eastern peak and carving stone is a logical operation of world-ordering—unifying script, law, and cosmos in one vertical act. The mountain becomes a billboard of sovereignty: Heaven is informed, the empire is standardized, time is restarted.", "logic_chain": "1) East/Taishan is the birth direction of yang and spring → 2) the First Emperor claims to have pacified the world → 3) Feng-Shan style ascent reports success to Heaven → 4) carved text freezes achievement beyond oral rumor → 5) standardized characters on stone model standardized realm → 6) conclusion: political unity must be cosmically announced and lithically archived.", "logic_practice": "1) For charts needing new cycles, use eastern/wood timing as ‘Taishan announcement’ of a new phase. 2) Career mandate years: treat major promotions as personal fengshan—public declaration + inner rectification. 3) Cultivation: climb metaphor—progressive ascent of essence-qi-spirit with written vows. 4) When Day Master is weak, ‘report to Heaven’ via modest ritual before expansion. 5) Study stele dates as training in converting reign years to sexagenary cycles.", "logic_compare": "More imperial-performative and unifying than temple miracle steles. Differs from 岱岳观造像记 by being sovereign proclamation rather than religious image-dedication economy." }, { "name_han": "姚伯多造像记", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: Northern Dynasties Buddhist (and hybrid) image inscriptions prove that carving a Buddha and recording donors’ names is a logical transfer of merit across family and rebirth—stone makes karma bankable. The text argues that public naming + image = contractual salvation technology.", "logic_chain": "1) Suffering is explained by karmic debt → 2) making an image generates merit → 3) inscription assigns merit to parents, kin, and realm → 4) visibility of names binds social prestige to piety → 5) permanent stone outlasts the donor’s life → 6) conclusion: religious art is an engineered ledger of intergenerational transfer.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi family luck, model ‘merit transfer’ as Resource/Seal shared among palace relations. 2) Remedies: dedicate concrete good acts to named people (not vague prayer). 3) Cultivation: combine visualization (image) with written intention (inscription logic). 4) For illness charts, pair medical action with merit practice without substituting one for the other. 5) Read donor lists as sociology of who seeks cosmic insurance in crisis eras.", "logic_compare": "Unlike pure Daoist mountain steles, it is merit-economy and image-based. Differs from 仙传外科 by seeking soteriological cure of rebirth, not clinical surgical technique." }, { "name_han": "岱岳观造像记碑", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: Daiyue Abbey image steles at Taishan prove that Daoist-Buddhist ritual institutions at the sacred mountain operate a continuous economy of dedication—imperial and local actors buy cosmic favor through images, dates, and offices. The mountain cult is shown as administrative-ritual infrastructure across dynasties.", "logic_chain": "1) Taishan already hosts imperial fengshan prestige → 2) abbeys and image halls localize that prestige for ongoing petitions → 3) dated dedications track political-religious patronage → 4) images embody deities as addressable persons → 5) repeated inscriptions create serial evidence of efficacy claims → 6) conclusion: sacred site power is maintained by institutional repetition, not one-time imperial ascent alone.", "logic_practice": "1) Treat ‘serial dedication’ as model for long-term BaZi remedies: repeated small rites over one dramatic act. 2) Map temple network logic onto chart: multiple useful gods must be fed in rotation. 3) Cultivation: fixed sacred schedule at a chosen ‘personal mountain’ (altar). 4) Historical BaZi: use stele dates to study cluster events (epidemics, wars, patronage waves). 5) Prefer institutional ethics—lineage, place, calendar—over charismatic one-off claims.", "logic_compare": "Unlike 泰山刻石’s singular sovereign boast, these are serial religious accounts. Unlike 姚伯多’s often family-merit focus, they sit inside a major mountain abbey’s continuous cult administration." }, { "name_han": "仙传外科集验方", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: ‘immortal-transmitted’ surgical formulas prove that external medicine can claim Daoist legitimacy without abandoning empirical procedure—sacred origin authorizes risky techniques while case experience verifies them. The text argues a dual logic: revelation for prestige, trial for efficacy.", "logic_chain": "1) Surgery is dangerous and socially sensitive → 2) immortal transmission frames it as higher knowledge → 3) collected formulas and cases show repeatable steps → 4) external treatment complements internal qi theories → 5) success stories convert stigma into craft → 6) conclusion: true ‘immortal’ medicine is lineage plus verified technique, not miracle alone.", "logic_practice": "1) In health BaZi, do not spiritualize away surgical indications; use chart for timing and support gods. 2) Metal/Fire balance: inflammation vs structure—map to external vs internal strategies. 3) Cultivation: body as temple—wound care ethics as purity practice. 4) Prefer methods with both lineage story and observed outcomes. 5) Day selection for procedures: avoid major clashes of the body palace when optional.", "logic_compare": "Unlike pure zhiguai healing tales, it is technical and formula-driven. Differs from 月波洞中记 by treating the body surgically rather than reading fate from bone/face structure alone." }, { "name_han": "月波洞中记", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: this physiognomy classic proves that destiny is legible in the structured landscape of the face and bones because the body is a condensed cosmograph—form is frozen qi. It argues that reading ‘mountains and waters’ on the visage yields probabilistic life patterns without needing birth data alone.", "logic_chain": "1) Heavenly pattern precipitates as human form → 2) facial zones correspond to life phases and relatives → 3) bone is structure (lingering fate), flesh/color is timing → 4) balanced clear features signal smooth qi flow → 5) breaks, scars, and murky color signal blockage or shock → 6) conclusion: morphology is a spatial BaZi that can corroborate or challenge the natal chart.", "logic_practice": "1) Use face reading as second channel to verify BaZi claims (career bone vs Officer stars). 2) Map forehead–midface–chin to early–middle–late luck like decade pillars. 3) Cultivation: improve ‘color’ (shenqi) via sleep, breath, virtue—mutable layer of fate. 4) Ethical practice: never condemn clients by a single feature; require multi-sign concurrence. 5) Combine with lunar/time gods: form = body, chart = schedule.", "logic_compare": "Unlike stele cult texts, it is technical anthropology of the body. Unlike fiction’s moral ghosts, it is diagnostic and morphological. Differs from 过山榜 by elite physiognomic system rather than ethnic charter myth." }, { "name_han": "过山榜", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: the Yao ‘Crossing-Mountain Warrant’ proves that ethnic survival rights are argued as a Heaven-granted charter from the ancient king-dog/Panhu myth—mobility, tax exemption, and mountain livelihood are logical consequences of a primordial covenant. The document is a portable constitution for a migrating people.", "logic_chain": "1) Origin myth establishes unique service to an ancient ruler → 2) reward is written as permanent privilege to live by mountains → 3) copies of the warrant travel with lineages → 4) presentation of the text negotiates with lowland states → 5) ritual song and festival keep the covenant emotionally binding → 6) conclusion: political ecology of the highlands is legitimated by sacred contract narrative.", "logic_practice": "1) In BaZi for mobility/migration cases, weight Traveling Horse and resource-from-mountain (Resource in Earth/Wood) as ‘crossing-mountain’ patterns. 2) Cultivation: treat personal ‘warrant’ as clear life vow—what you are allowed to do without self-betrayal. 3) Ritual: renew covenant annually (as Yao festivals renew). 4) Legal-spiritual analogy: written intention protects practice boundaries. 5) Read community charts/history via shared myths of exemption and hardship.", "logic_compare": "Unlike imperial 符瑞 books, the warrant serves a minority’s negotiation with empire, not the emperor’s mandate alone. Differs from 盘王大歌 by being a charter/document logic more than a full ritual epic performance." }, { "name_han": "盘王大歌", "logic_thesis": "Core argument: the great songs of King Pan prove that cosmology, migration memory, and moral order are transmitted as sung epic—sound is the storage medium of law. Performing the cycle re-creates the world and reinstalls the people inside it; forgetting the song is civilizational amnesia.", "logic_chain": "1) Origins of world and people are narrated in verse → 2) verse is inseparable from ritual occasion → 3) communal singing synchronizes memory and emotion → 4) taboos and ethics are embedded in narrative episodes → 5) each performance updates belonging for the living → 6) conclusion: oral-ritual epic is a living constitution of cosmos and kin.", "logic_practice": "1) BaZi counseling as ‘song of the chart’: narrate luck cycles as chapters, not isolated gods. 2) Cultivation: chanting/mantra as 盘王 method—rhythm binds intention. 3) Ancestral work: seasonal recitation of family history as qi repair. 4) For group rituals, prioritize synchronized voice over private visualization alone. 5) Study how repeated narrative heals migration trauma—apply to clients with multiple moves/clashes of home palace.", "logic_compare": "Unlike 过山榜’s documentary warrant, the songs are performative cosmology. Unlike literati zhiguai, they are communal, ethnic, and liturgical rather than individual strange anecdotes for reading pleasure." } ] }
thought: The user wants me to extract logical reasoning from 20 classical Chinese texts related to BaZi/Daoist scholarship. They want a structured JSON output with specific fields for each text.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: sacred geography and stele-writing prove that mountain-temple cults are not mere local piety but official-cosmic contracts binding Heaven, Earth, and the state. The text demonstrates that ritual inscription at Zhongyue (Songshan) legitimizes both Daoist lineage and imperial authority by making the mountain a permanent witness of cosmic order.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Songshan is the central peak among the Five Sacred Mountains → 2) therefore it mediates the axis of Heaven–Earth qi → 3) a stele at the Lingmiao records offerings and revelations as public evidence → 4) evidence of numinous response (lingying) proves the mountain’s agency → 5) agency of the mountain validates the cult and the sponsors’ virtue → 6) conclusion: political and spiritual legitimacy flow from correctly situating ritual at the cosmic center.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, treat ‘center’ (Earth, ji-wu) as the pivot that balances other stems; diagnose when center qi is missing or over-strong. 2) For cultivation, use Songshan/central-mountain imagery as a meditation axis (middle dantian / yellow court). 3) When reading temple omens or ‘response’ stories, map them to day-master resonance with Earth/central palace. 4) Prefer stele-style dating (year, stem-branch, ritual intent) when reconstructing historical charts. 5) Use ‘inscription as contract’ logic: a vow or talisman is only valid if place, time, and sponsor virtue align.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike the West Peak Huashan stele, which emphasizes martial-apotropaic and border-mountain power, this text centers axial/central mediation. Unlike pure Daoist hagiography, it is a public stone contract between cult, mountain, and polity—hence more juridical and cosmographic than narrative.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: encyclopedic classification of the Dao proves that the Way is not one school’s monopoly but a state-legible system of categories—immortals, methods, mountains, texts—through which power and knowledge are ordered. Compilation itself is an argument: gathering quotations demonstrates that Daoist authority is cumulative, textual, and administrable.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Imperial encyclopedias aim to totalize useful knowledge → 2) a ‘Dao section’ isolates religious-technical material as a bureaucratic genus → 3) excerpts from multiple eras are juxtaposed without one sect’s monopoly → 4) juxtaposition implies commensurability of Daoist claims under court taxonomy → 5) taxonomy allows selection of methods/precedents for rule and self-cultivation → 6) conclusion: the Dao becomes a curated archive of techniques and exempla, not only private mystery.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Build BaZi ‘libraries’ the same way: stem-branch, gods, patterns as cross-referenced categories, not single-book dogma. 2) When a chart rule conflicts, treat sources as leishu layers—older stratum vs later gloss. 3) Practice method-selection: match client need to the right Dao-entry (fate, health, timing), as the encyclopedia matches topic to extract. 4) Use citation discipline: every claim should name a lineage/source layer. 5) For cultivation, rotate techniques (breath, diet, spirit-travel) as modular entries, not one absolute path.
entries.logic_compare: Differs from 艺文类聚·灵异部 by framing the Dao as a technical-administrative domain rather than marvels for literary display. Differs from later fiction anthologies by claiming court-level knowledge control instead of entertainment or moral parable.

The section argues that legitimacy is not abstract philosophy but a feedback loop of sign → interpretation → ritual/policy.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Heaven communicates through irregular phenomena → 2) only the sovereign is the proper addressee of those signs → 3) officials archive and classify signs as evidence of virtue or warning → 4) correct recognition and response reaffirm the mandate → 5) misreading or ignoring signs justifies critique or crisis → 6) conclusion: political time is omen-time; history is a ledger of cosmic replies.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi yearly luck, treat ‘unusual’ combinations (void, clash of key gods) as fuyui requiring response, not fatalism. 2) Practice omen protocol: observe → classify (auspicious/warning) → act (remedy, timing, conduct). 3) Map imperial ‘response rites’ onto personal cultivation (confession, offering, schedule change). 4) When charts show strong Fire/Heaven-official patterns, weight public reputation and mandate-like career signs. 5) Train interpretation ethics: do not invent omens; read only what the chart actually produces.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 玉海·郊祀, which focuses on standardized state sacrifice, this text prioritizes extraordinary signs as proof of mandate. Unlike literary 灵异 collections, its purpose is statecraft historiography, not wonder or fiction.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: suburban sacrifice (jiaosi) proves that cosmic order is maintained by calendarized, graded ritual to Heaven and Earth rather than by ad hoc devotion. The text demonstrates that correct space (south suburb), time (solstice cycles), and rank of offering are the logical conditions of political-cosmic equilibrium.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Heaven and Earth require periodic, formal address → 2) the south suburb is the spatial analog of Heaven’s seat → 3) solstice and seasonal nodes are the temporal keys → 4) ritual ranks and utensils encode hierarchy of cosmos and court → 5) when form is complete, qi and politics realign → 6) conclusion: cosmic stability is a function of exact ritual geometry and timing.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Align BaZi remedies and offerings with solar terms (jieqi), not only lunar festivals. 2) Treat day-master ‘audience with Heaven’ as jiaosi: use hours/directions that match the chart’s noble gods. 3) For cultivation, schedule major work at winter/summer solstice poles (yin-yang extremes). 4) Design ritual space: facing, height, purity rules as micro-jiaosi. 5) Diagnose disorder as mis-timed or mis-ranked action (wrong god, wrong season).
entries.logic_compare: Differs from 符瑞 by stressing regular liturgy over irregular omen. Differs from mountain steles by locating the main cosmic contract at the capital’s ritual periphery rather than at a sacred peak.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: a late Ming leishu proves that ‘Heaven’s center’ knowledge is a collage of classical, historical, and marvel materials organized for retrieval—authority comes from breadth of citation and topical order. It argues that understanding the world is indexing: names, places, anomalies, and arts become usable only when cross-filed.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Knowledge is scattered across genres → 2) encyclopedic topicalization re-centers it under usable heads → 3) inclusion of marvels alongside institutions treats anomaly as data → 4) data without narrative closure invites comparative reading → 5) comparative reading yields practical precedents → 6) conclusion: wisdom is an ordered archive under Heaven’s canopy, not a single revealed book.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Build personal BaZi case indices by topic (marriage, illness, wealth) like leishu entries. 2) When stuck on a chart, open parallel ‘entries’: classical rule, historical analog, folk case. 3) Treat strange chart phenomena as 天中记-style data, then seek pattern frequency. 4) Practice citation hygiene: every technique tagged by source period. 5) Use ‘center of Heaven’ as a metaphor for the chart’s balance point (middle qi / mediator stem).
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 太平御览, it is later, denser with Ming interests and marvels, less purely imperial-bureaucratic. Compared with pure fiction collections, it still claims encyclopedic utility rather than story art alone.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: collecting ‘numinous anomalies’ for literary encyclopedias proves that the strange is a category of culture useful for rhetoric, omen literacy, and moral illustration—not only for priests. The section demonstrates that anomaly becomes classical capital when excerpted and re-usable.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Literature needs figures of the uncanny → 2) court compilers excerpt historical and legendary marvels → 3) marvels are sorted as a genus (lingyi) → 4) genus status makes them teachable and citable → 5) citation in essays/poetry trains readers to read signs → 6) conclusion: the supernatural is domesticated into elite knowledge through anthology form.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Train BaZi intuition on classical ‘strange correspondences’ (dreams, animals, weather) as symbolic language. 2) Separate literary omen from technical rule: use 灵异 for metaphor, classics for calculation. 3) In client counseling, use story exempla to explain clash/combine without fatalism. 4) Catalog recurring anomaly motifs against ten-gods patterns. 5) Practice critical filter: aesthetic value ≠ predictive validity.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 册府符瑞, it serves literary culture more than mandate politics. Unlike Qing zhiguai fiction, it is excerpt-based and non-novelistic, aiming at classifiable snippets for composition.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: early Ming chuanqi proves that after dynastic rupture, the underworld, ghosts, and retributive law become the narrative court where human justice fails—fiction argues that moral causality is stricter than official law. Love and exam ambition are tested against ghostly contract and karmic ledger.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Human courts and exams are corruptible → 2) the dead and spirits retain memory of debt and vow → 3) narrative stages encounters that enforce unpaid justice → 4) protagonists who honor vows/rituals survive or transform → 5) those who break faith suffer retributive plot turns → 6) conclusion: ethical law is cosmic; fiction is its courtroom drama.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi ethics counseling, stress vow-keeping and debt-clearing as luck factors (not only gods). 2) Read Peach Blossom / Officer patterns with 剪灯-style caution: desire without ritual form invites ghostly backlash metaphors. 3) Use story structure for timing: crisis → ritual recognition → resolution as luck-cycle template. 4) For cultivation, practice ‘clearing unfinished business’ (apology, offering, ending false vows). 5) Distinguish entertainment omen from chart evidence when clients bring ghost dreams.
entries.logic_compare: More structured and literati than later oral-flavored Qing zhiguai; less encyclopedic than leishu. Differs from 耳食录 by stronger early-Ming exam-and-ghost moral architecture rather than Qing social satire.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: Qing ‘hearsay’ tales prove that social rumor and strange events are a diagnostic mirror of class hypocrisy, desire, and local power—truth is what people dare only say as ghost story. The text argues that the supernatural is a coded sociology.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Direct critique of officials/customs is risky → 2) hearsay frame distances the author → 3) spirits, foxes, and anomalies act out social tensions → 4) readers decode moral targets from plot outcomes → 5) ‘ear-eating’ (credulous listening) is both method and warning → 6) conclusion: strange tales are a critical epistemology of Qing society.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When charts show strong Seal/Officer imbalance, look for social-role stress (as in 耳食 satire). 2) Treat client anecdotes as hearsay data: useful, biased, to be verified against stems-branches. 3) Use fox/ghost motifs as metaphors for hidden attachments and parasitism in relationships. 4) Practice ethical listening without superstition inflation. 5) For cultivation, purify ‘hearsay mind’—don’t let rumor qi steer decisions.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 剪灯新话’s elegant chuanqi of retribution, it is more anecdotal and socially pointed. Unlike 谐铎, it is less systematically ‘bell of harmony’ moral essay-tale hybrid.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: ‘the harmonious bell’ proves that comedy, irony, and strange episodes can ring a moral alarm louder than solemn preaching—wit is a logical instrument of reform. The collection argues that exposing absurdity realigns human conduct with cosmic decency.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Didactic seriousness often fails to change behavior → 2) humorous or bizarre frames lower defenses → 3) punchline reveals ethical inversion → 4) inversion shocks the reader into revaluation → 5) revaluation is the true ‘sounding of the bell’ → 6) conclusion: satire is a spiritual technology of awakening.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In counseling, use gentle irony to break fatalistic BaZi readings without shaming. 2) Map ‘absurd outcomes’ in charts (wealth god hurting self) as 谐铎 inversions teaching balance. 3) Cultivation practice: daily ‘bell’—one honest laugh at ego’s tricks. 4) When Hurt Officer is strong, channel it into constructive critique, not chaos. 5) Prefer corrective stories over scare tactics in ethical timing advice.
entries.logic_compare: More intentionally satirical-moral than 夜雨秋灯录’s sentimental/strange romance. Differs from 耳食录 by a clearer program of ‘sounding the bell’ reform through wit.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: late Qing tale-collections under rain-and-lamp atmosphere prove that emotion, fate, and the uncanny intertwine in a world of social decline—feeling (qing) itself becomes a causal force. The text argues that destiny is experienced as night-listening: partial, intimate, and rain-blurred.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Public institutions weaken in late Qing imagination → 2) private rooms (lamp, rain) become sites of revelation → 3) ghosts and coincidences answer suppressed emotions → 4) narrative prioritizes pathos over system → 5) pathos trains readers to see fate as lived texture → 6) conclusion: cosmic pattern is known through affective encounter, not only through official omen tables.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Weight emotional houses (Spouse, Peer, Output) carefully in late-style ‘qing’ cases. 2) Night-hour charts / yin gods: use gentle language, not harsh decree. 3) Cultivation: rain-lamp meditation—observe arising images without grasping. 4) Timing advice for grief years: ritual + rest, not aggressive remedy stacking. 5) Convert story pathos into chart factors (void, clash of resource/seal as loneliness markers).
entries.logic_compare: More lyrical and late-Qing than early Ming 剪灯. Less purely satirical than 谐铎; more ‘mood of decline’ than 萤窗异草’s often ornate romance-anomaly craft.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: Yu Yue’s notes prove that literati skepticism and documentary habit can host the strange without surrendering critical judgment—anomaly is recorded as problem for reason. The text argues for a scholarly middle path: neither credulous fangshi nor pure denial.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Elite learning prizes evidence and philology → 2) strange reports still circulate among officials and scholars → 3) notebook form allows provisional storage without dogma → 4) commentary weighs probability and motive → 5) residual unexplained cases remain open → 6) conclusion: rational culture strengthens itself by carefully archiving the residual.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Adopt 右台 method in BaZi: record cases, mark confidence levels, revise. 2) Separate observation, inference, and client belief in write-ups. 3) Cultivation: ‘notebook mind’—register experiences without inflating them into enlightenment claims. 4) When classic rules fail, archive counterexamples instead of forcing fit. 5) Prefer provisional language in predictions (ranges, conditions).
entries.logic_compare: More scholarly and restrained than commercial zhiguai like 夜雨秋灯录. Differs from imperial omen books by personal literati epistemology rather than mandate ideology.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: ‘strange grasses by the firefly window’ proves that Qing talent-and-beauty aesthetics can absorb the supernatural into refined narrative craft—anomaly serves romance, talent, and fate of the refined self. It argues that destiny is readable in the chemistry of qing, talent, and otherworldly aid or trial.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Literati identity centers talent and sentiment → 2) foxes/immortals/ghosts become partners or examiners of that identity → 3) plots test constancy of feeling and study → 4) otherworldly reward or punishment ratifies human worth → 5) ornamental prose elevates the strange to art → 6) conclusion: the cosmos sponsors refined self-realization when qing and talent align.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For charts with strong Output + Peach Blossom, read ‘talent-qing’ paths carefully. 2) Treat ‘immortal aid’ motifs as Resource/Seal support patterns. 3) Cultivation: firefly-window practice—short night sessions of study + calm breath. 4) Warn against romanticizing spirit-relationships when Officer/Kill is unstable. 5) Use story arcs to explain ten-year luck as chapters of trial and recognition.
entries.logic_compare: More ornate and romance-centered than 耳食录’s social hearsay; less encyclopedic than leishu. Compared with 剪灯新话, it is Qing taste—longer on sentiment and polish than early-Ming moral court-of-ghosts structure.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: the Huashan temple stele proves that the Western Peak is a juridical-numinous power that polices borders of life, death, and imperial space—stone text makes the mountain an enforcer of oaths and a guarantor of regional order. Legitimacy is forged by naming the mountain’s office and past responses.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Huashan occupies the west metal position in the Five Peaks system → 2) west encodes weapons, autumn, judgment, and boundary → 3) temple cult archives petitions and miracles → 4) stele freezes that archive into permanent law-like memory → 5) rulers and locals both claim protection under that memory → 6) conclusion: sacred mountain office is a political-cosmic police power, not mere scenery.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, link strong Metal / west / You-Xu patterns to Huashan-type ‘judgment and boundary’ themes. 2) Oath and contract work: use metal hours/directions for cutting bad ties. 3) Cultivation: white-metal breathing, decluttering, decisive endings. 4) Remedies for chaotic Peach Blossom: invoke ‘boundary god’ logic—clear rules. 5) Historical dating of events: match stele years to stem-branch for macro cases.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike Zhongyue’s central-axis mediation, Huashan stresses western martial-legal numen. Unlike Taishan’s imperial tour inscriptions, it is temple-cult and regional-oath focused as much as imperial cosmology.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: Qin (and related) Taishan inscriptions prove that ascending the eastern peak and carving stone is a logical operation of world-ordering—unifying script, law, and cosmos in one vertical act. The mountain becomes a billboard of sovereignty: Heaven is informed, the empire is standardized, time is restarted.
entries.logic_chain: 1) East/Taishan is the birth direction of yang and spring → 2) the First Emperor claims to have pacified the world → 3) Feng-Shan style ascent reports success to Heaven → 4) carved text freezes achievement beyond oral rumor → 5) standardized characters on stone model standardized realm → 6) conclusion: political unity must be cosmically announced and lithically archived.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For charts needing new cycles, use eastern/wood timing as ‘Taishan announcement’ of a new phase. 2) Career mandate years: treat major promotions as personal fengshan—public declaration + inner rectification. 3) Cultivation: climb metaphor—progressive ascent of essence-qi-spirit with written vows. 4) When Day Master is weak, ‘report to Heaven’ via modest ritual before expansion. 5) Study stele dates as training in converting reign years to sexagenary cycles.
entries.logic_compare: More imperial-performative and unifying than temple miracle steles. Differs from 岱岳观造像记 by being sovereign proclamation rather than religious image-dedication economy.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: Northern Dynasties Buddhist (and hybrid) image inscriptions prove that carving a Buddha and recording donors’ names is a logical transfer of merit across family and rebirth—stone makes karma bankable. The text argues that public naming + image = contractual salvation technology.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Suffering is explained by karmic debt → 2) making an image generates merit → 3) inscription assigns merit to parents, kin, and realm → 4) visibility of names binds social prestige to piety → 5) permanent stone outlasts the donor’s life → 6) conclusion: religious art is an engineered ledger of intergenerational transfer.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi family luck, model ‘merit transfer’ as Resource/Seal shared among palace relations. 2) Remedies: dedicate concrete good acts to named people (not vague prayer). 3) Cultivation: combine visualization (image) with written intention (inscription logic). 4) For illness charts, pair medical action with merit practice without substituting one for the other. 5) Read donor lists as sociology of who seeks cosmic insurance in crisis eras.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Daoist mountain steles, it is merit-economy and image-based. Differs from 仙传外科 by seeking soteriological cure of rebirth, not clinical surgical technique.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: Daiyue Abbey image steles at Taishan prove that Daoist-Buddhist ritual institutions at the sacred mountain operate a continuous economy of dedication—imperial and local actors buy cosmic favor through images, dates, and offices. The mountain cult is shown as administrative-ritual infrastructure across dynasties.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Taishan already hosts imperial fengshan prestige → 2) abbeys and image halls localize that prestige for ongoing petitions → 3) dated dedications track political-religious patronage → 4) images embody deities as addressable persons → 5) repeated inscriptions create serial evidence of efficacy claims → 6) conclusion: sacred site power is maintained by institutional repetition, not one-time imperial ascent alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat ‘serial dedication’ as model for long-term BaZi remedies: repeated small rites over one dramatic act. 2) Map temple network logic onto chart: multiple useful gods must be fed in rotation. 3) Cultivation: fixed sacred schedule at a chosen ‘personal mountain’ (altar). 4) Historical BaZi: use stele dates to study cluster events (epidemics, wars, patronage waves). 5) Prefer institutional ethics—lineage, place, calendar—over charismatic one-off claims.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 泰山刻石’s singular sovereign boast, these are serial religious accounts. Unlike 姚伯多’s often family-merit focus, they sit inside a major mountain abbey’s continuous cult administration.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: ‘immortal-transmitted’ surgical formulas prove that external medicine can claim Daoist legitimacy without abandoning empirical procedure—sacred origin authorizes risky techniques while case experience verifies them. The text argues a dual logic: revelation for prestige, trial for efficacy.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Surgery is dangerous and socially sensitive → 2) immortal transmission frames it as higher knowledge → 3) collected formulas and cases show repeatable steps → 4) external treatment complements internal qi theories → 5) success stories convert stigma into craft → 6) conclusion: true ‘immortal’ medicine is lineage plus verified technique, not miracle alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In health BaZi, do not spiritualize away surgical indications; use chart for timing and support gods. 2) Metal/Fire balance: inflammation vs structure—map to external vs internal strategies. 3) Cultivation: body as temple—wound care ethics as purity practice. 4) Prefer methods with both lineage story and observed outcomes. 5) Day selection for procedures: avoid major clashes of the body palace when optional.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure zhiguai healing tales, it is technical and formula-driven. Differs from 月波洞中记 by treating the body surgically rather than reading fate from bone/face structure alone.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: this physiognomy classic proves that destiny is legible in the structured landscape of the face and bones because the body is a condensed cosmograph—form is frozen qi. It argues that reading ‘mountains and waters’ on the visage yields probabilistic life patterns without needing birth data alone.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Heavenly pattern precipitates as human form → 2) facial zones correspond to life phases and relatives → 3) bone is structure (lingering fate), flesh/color is timing → 4) balanced clear features signal smooth qi flow → 5) breaks, scars, and murky color signal blockage or shock → 6) conclusion: morphology is a spatial BaZi that can corroborate or challenge the natal chart.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Use face reading as second channel to verify BaZi claims (career bone vs Officer stars). 2) Map forehead–midface–chin to early–middle–late luck like decade pillars. 3) Cultivation: improve ‘color’ (shenqi) via sleep, breath, virtue—mutable layer of fate. 4) Ethical practice: never condemn clients by a single feature; require multi-sign concurrence. 5) Combine with lunar/time gods: form = body, chart = schedule.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike stele cult texts, it is technical anthropology of the body. Unlike fiction’s moral ghosts, it is diagnostic and morphological. Differs from 过山榜 by elite physiognomic system rather than ethnic charter myth.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: the Yao ‘Crossing-Mountain Warrant’ proves that ethnic survival rights are argued as a Heaven-granted charter from the ancient king-dog/Panhu myth—mobility, tax exemption, and mountain livelihood are logical consequences of a primordial covenant. The document is a portable constitution for a migrating people.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Origin myth establishes unique service to an ancient ruler → 2) reward is written as permanent privilege to live by mountains → 3) copies of the warrant travel with lineages → 4) presentation of the text negotiates with lowland states → 5) ritual song and festival keep the covenant emotionally binding → 6) conclusion: political ecology of the highlands is legitimated by sacred contract narrative.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi for mobility/migration cases, weight Traveling Horse and resource-from-mountain (Resource in Earth/Wood) as ‘crossing-mountain’ patterns. 2) Cultivation: treat personal ‘warrant’ as clear life vow—what you are allowed to do without self-betrayal. 3) Ritual: renew covenant annually (as Yao festivals renew). 4) Legal-spiritual analogy: written intention protects practice boundaries. 5) Read community charts/history via shared myths of exemption and hardship.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike imperial 符瑞 books, the warrant serves a minority’s negotiation with empire, not the emperor’s mandate alone. Differs from 盘王大歌 by being a charter/document logic more than a full ritual epic performance.

entries.logic_thesis: Core argument: the great songs of King Pan prove that cosmology, migration memory, and moral order are transmitted as sung epic—sound is the storage medium of law. Performing the cycle re-creates the world and reinstalls the people inside it; forgetting the song is civilizational amnesia.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Origins of world and people are narrated in verse → 2) verse is inseparable from ritual occasion → 3) communal singing synchronizes memory and emotion → 4) taboos and ethics are embedded in narrative episodes → 5) each performance updates belonging for the living → 6) conclusion: oral-ritual epic is a living constitution of cosmos and kin.
entries.logic_practice: 1) BaZi counseling as ‘song of the chart’: narrate luck cycles as chapters, not isolated gods. 2) Cultivation: chanting/mantra as 盘王 method—rhythm binds intention. 3) Ancestral work: seasonal recitation of family history as qi repair. 4) For group rituals, prioritize synchronized voice over private visualization alone. 5) Study how repeated narrative heals migration trauma—apply to clients with multiple moves/clashes of home palace.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 过山榜’s documentary warrant, the songs are performative cosmology. Unlike literati zhiguai, they are communal, ethnic, and liturgical rather than individual strange anecdotes for reading pleasure.
